evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Every truck gets a door and a time.' plus lede 'Dockline is a dock appointment app for mid-size warehouses. You publish slots on your doors; carriers' dispatchers book an arrival time instead of calling in and waiting in the yard.' names what, who and both sides. 'Book a demo' sits beside '30 minutes, online. Bring your door count and receiving hours.' As the ops manager I could repeat it after the first screen.
evidence.fit: Warehouse path: demo CTA 5 times, all to https://dockline.example/demo; gate receiving list, slot-rules sheet, and a pricing/setup/'what it leaves alone' block (WMS/TMS untouched, no integration needed) answer an ops manager's doubts. Dispatcher path: nav 'Carriers: book a slot' and the closing note go to https://book.dockline.example, and the 'Dispatchers book from a link' section says no accounts, no app. Weak spot: at 390 the dispatcher link is only inside Menu and at the bottom of the page, so a dispatcher landing on a phone doesn't see their path on the first screen. Pilot status (two unnamed, no results) is stated under the hero.
evidence.distinctiveness: The hero artifact is a drawn dock face with six numbered doors, trailers with carrier names on the nose, and red/green dock lights driven by a 'Yard clock' slider. Below it are a gate-shack receiving list and a per-door rules sheet with 'Hold after start'. None of this is the stock SaaS kit. Lower sections (three-column facts, final CTA) are plainer.
evidence.proof: 1440: the booking grid and yard clock fill the right half of the first screen, and I booked Door 3 10:00 without scrolling. The gate list is explicitly 'the same sample day as the grid above, read at 09:30'. Inconsistencies a dock person would notice: the static confirmation card puts 'Keller Trucking · 53' dry van' on Door 3, which the rules sheet calls Reefer. Door 6 is 'Outbound pickups / Closed to inbound' yet shows bookable inbound 'Open' hours. Copy says 'The page only offers doors that take the trailer type', but the demo form let me book any trailer on any door.
evidence.craft: 1440: the header 'Book a demo' renders near-black text (rgb 23,26,29) on green (21,122,58), about 3:1 contrast, and axe flags one color-contrast node. I entered a 40-character carrier name and the Door 3 cell grew to six lines, stretching the whole 10:00 row. The rest holds a clear type scale, mono hours and a consistent grid, with no overflow at 320/390/768/1440 (probe).
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed rather than shrunk. Door tabs 1–6 switch the grid to one full-width column ('Door 3: 4 open hours left today' announced). Tapping Door 3 10:00 scrolled the booking sheet into view with the Carrier field focused, and the confirmation appeared in the same spot. Menu opens and closes and lists all links. Header Book-a-demo is hidden at 390, but the hero button is in view. Slot rules table restacks into labelled rows.
evidence.honesty: Pilot disclosure is in the hero: 'two mid-size warehouses we can't name yet, with no measured results'. The demo says 'The booking stays in this page; nothing is sent' before you act. Gate list caption: 'Carriers and references are invented'. Footer: 'In pilot; not yet generally available'. Pricing says plainly that there is no public price list. Deductions: the trailer-type claim isn't true of the demo, and the confirmation panel contains 'The wording is ours to confirm with the client', a builder's note that reads oddly to a visitor.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390. Clicking a passed slot gives '06:00 at Door 2 has passed on the yard clock (09:30). Move the clock earlier...'. An empty submit gives 'Enter the carrier name so the gate knows who to expect.' Booking produces reference DL-UZFY, the cell turns 'yours' and an SMS preview appears. Escape closes the sheet and returns focus to the slot. Clock to 06:30 moves 3 trailers in and opens 29 hours; clock to 16:00 leaves 0 open. 'Reset the sample day' restores Door 3 10:00 to Open. 'Book another hour' moves focus to the next open slot. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific nouns: 'gate shack', 'Hold after start', 'Floor-loaded freight adds a second hour', 'no dock leveler', 'it does not move trailers or receive freight'. Long, explanatory H2s ('The gate sees who is due, at which door, and who is running late') read flatter than they need to. The leaked line 'The wording is ours to confirm with the client' in the confirmation is a real defect.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, named audience, demo CTA with what-to-bring, pilot note, and the operable grid with trailers at doors all in one viewport. 390: promise, lede, Book a demo with duration, pilot note and the yard clock are in view. evidence.honesty: The pilots section is candid ('Neither has agreed to be named... We also don't have numbers to show you yet. Nothing here is a real carrier.' and the form says 'Nothing you enter leaves this page.' However, the page also states unmeasured outcomes as fact: 'Dispatchers book in under a minute', 'the booking takes twenty seconds', 'Setup takes about an hour', and an unlabelled 3h35-vs-8-min story. 'A dry van can't book the reefer door by mistake' is false in the demo: I booked a 53' reefer on live-unload Door 1, and a dry van can be chosen for Door 5.

evidence.copy: The best words on either page: 'laminated sheet at the guard shack', 'Drop-and-hook, no lumper', 'so one broker can't take every morning window on a Monday', 'When a carrier sends a detention invoice, you have the gate stamp', 'the driver is told to rebook, not to park'. evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, Book a demo, Try the board and the dispatcher link are in view, but only the board's header and two door rows show at the bottom edge, with a large empty right half. 390: headline, lede, both CTAs, the dispatcher link and the board title are in view, and the board rows show past windows only. The promise is specific; what makes it believable is only partly in view.

problems: At 390 the board is a desktop Gantt in a sideways scroller: no open window is visible without a horizontal swipe, open targets are 37px wide, and there is no pointer to 'now'. The dispatcher, the audience that must find it easy, gets the weakest version of the artifact.

Unmeasured outcomes are stated as fact on a page that says it has no numbers: 'book in under a minute', 'takes twenty seconds', 'Setup takes about an hour', and the unlabelled '3h35 vs eight minutes in the yard' story.

Demo contradicts copy and has rough edges: a reefer books onto live-unload Door 1 despite 'A dry van can't book the reefer door by mistake'; the now-line overlaps Door 3's block; 'Tuesday 21 Oct' is a Wednesday; there is no reset and Escape doesn't close the drawer.

reason: As the ops manager on a laptop and the dispatcher on a phone, A's sample day works at every width: door tabs at 390, a clock that moves trucks, reset and clear errors. It also answers the cost and 'what does it touch' doubts. B's phone board hides every open window behind a sideways swipe, and B states speed and setup times it cannot back. B has the more dock-literate copy and the better dispatcher signposting in the hero; if the dispatcher's first-screen path were weighted above the working demo, or if A's leaked 'ours to confirm with the client' note and dry-van-at-reefer-door ticket counted as disqualifying for a founder, I would switch to B.
